title: Script class must be named exactly like its .cs file
description: A C# script resource resolves to the top-level partial class whose name equals the file name (case-sensitive); a mismatch is silently skipped at build time and surfaces only on instantiation as a generic "associated class could not be found" error that build and assembly-name problems also produce; the docs still quote an error text the engine no longer emits.
example: // Player.cs: public partial class PlayerController : CharacterBody2D {}  -> attaching Player.cs fails at run time
evidence_issues: #15661 (open, 43 reactions, 53 comments: proposal to attach a C# class by name instead of source path) | #71735 (closed, 0 reactions, 26 comments) | #66419 (closed, 0 reactions, 11 comments) | #74146 (closed not planned, 9 comments) | #85292 (open, 0 reactions, 3 comments: same-named partial files)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "Attached C# scripts should refer to a class that has a class name that matches the file name." and (stale) "Cannot find class XXX for script res://XXX.cs" | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html "the class Godot will use is the one named like the .cs file itself" | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_global_classes.html "The file name must match the class name in case-sensitive fashion."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs:54-56 (classes whose name differs from the file name are dropped, no diagnostic) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2550-2551 (actual run-time message "...contains a class definition with a name that matches the filename of the script exactly (it's case-sensitive)"; "Cannot find class" occurs nowhere in modules/mono) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:393-400 (editor derives the class name from the file name in validate_path)
frequency: 22 godotengine/godot issues contain the phrase "associated class could not be found" (GitHub search over all labels, 2026-10-23; causes are mixed) | at least 6 forum.godotengine.org threads with that error on one web-search page | #15661 43 reactions
fix_reason: Petrichor can make the file itself the class (GDScript model) or derive the class name from the path, leaving no second name to mismatch; if an explicit name is kept, the compiler rejects a mismatch (T).

title: Global class names are flat: C# namespaces are dropped
description: [GlobalClass] registers the bare type name without its namespace into the engine's single global-class map, so two namespaced classes with the same name, or a class named like an engine class, collide silently (an existing entry is overwritten, or the class is hidden from pickers with no warning).
example: namespace A { [GlobalClass] public partial class Item : Resource {} }  and  namespace B { [GlobalClass] public partial class Item : Resource {} }
evidence_issues: #95406 (open/reopened, 0 reactions, 2 comments: [GlobalClass] named like a built-in class is hidden from pickers; no warning even for a real collision such as Node3D) | #20610 (closed, 7 reactions, 12 comments: Godot C# types moved to a namespace to avoid name collisions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_global_classes.html "The MyNode type will be registered as a global class with the same name as the type's name."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:279 (global name = scriptType.Name, namespace dropped) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:53-57 (class_name hints also use the bare Name) | core/object/script_language.cpp:408-431 (ScriptServer::add_global_class keeps one flat StringName map; an existing entry is updated in place, no check against ClassDB) | editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:2564-2582 (registration path has no collision check)
frequency: low: only #95406 found on topic (GitHub search "GlobalClass namespace", 20 hits)
fix_reason: The Petrichor compiler can see all global names (ClassDB plus the global class cache) and reject collisions, and can map module-qualified names to unique global names; namespaced entries in the engine's own registry would need a core change.

title: Only one top-level class per file becomes a script
description: The generator gives a res:// script path only to the non-nested partial class named like the file; nested Godot classes and other classes in the file get no path (they cannot be attached in the editor or referenced from scenes), and a partial class split over same-named files in different folders registers only one path.
example: // Enemy.cs: public partial class Enemy : Node { public partial class Hitbox : Area2D {} }  -> Hitbox cannot be attached to a node
evidence_issues: #85292 (open, 0 reactions, 3 comments: partial Main.cs in two folders -> class not found) | #81683 (closed by PR #124305 in 4.8, 2 reactions, 7 comments: members of a nested GodotObject missing in GDScript completion) | #104268 (closed by PR #104279 in 4.5: Godot class nested in a generic class broke the generator) | #83071 (closed: generator broke with more than 2 nesting levels)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/diagnostics/GD0003.html (GD0003; generator text "A script file must only contain one class with a name that matches the file name.")
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs:43-44 (nested classes ignored) | ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs:47-52 (non-partial classes skipped) | ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs:98-106 (GD0003 when a second class maps to the same path) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/Common.cs:30-38 (GD0003 text) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:306-313 (only the first ScriptPathAttribute of a type is registered) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ClassPartialModifierAnalyzer.cs:39-53 (GD0001/GD0002 when partial is missing)
frequency: low: 13 topic:dotnet issues match "nested class" (GitHub search); each 0-3 reactions
fix_reason: Petrichor defines the script unit itself (file = class; inner classes either have a defined engine-addressable identity or are declared non-attachable) and the compiler reports any declaration that would silently not become a script.

title: Generic C# classes are only half scripts
description: An open generic Godot class has a script file but cannot be instantiated, attached, made [GlobalClass] or exported; each closed type gets a synthetic csharp:// path at run time, and this bookkeeping has produced registration and reload errors.
example: public partial class Pool<T> : Node where T : Node {}  public partial class EnemyPool : Pool<Enemy> {}
evidence_issues: #79519 (closed by PR #87550 in 4.3, 27 reactions, 28 comments; same duplicate-key error reported again on 4.5 in 2025-09/10 comments) | #74960 (open, 6 reactions, 5 comments: generic-typed members cannot be exported) | #110784 (open, 3 reactions: assembly unload fails when generic and non-generic classes share a name) | #102057 (open, 1 reaction: Resource deriving from a generic class shows "inspector might be out of date") | #15661 (open, 43 reactions; comments ask for generic nodes)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/diagnostics/GD0402.html (GD0402 "The class must not be generic. Make the class non-generic, or remove the '[GlobalClass]' attribute.")
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.h:137-139 (TypeInfo::can_instantiate is false for a generic type definition) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:577-590 (closed generic types get virtual path csharp://<path>:<type>.cs) | ScriptManagerBridge.cs:211-216 (generic scripts cannot be global classes) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/Common.cs:220-228 and GlobalClassAnalyzer.cs:31-34 (GD0402)
frequency: 35 topic:dotnet issues have "generic" in the title (GitHub search); #79519 27 reactions
status: open (#79519 fixed in 4.3, regressions reported on 4.5)
fix_reason: Specific to .NET generics; Petrichor generics face the same identity question -> L: forbid generic script classes or define that only closed instantiations are scripts with a stable engine-visible name; virtual script paths, if needed, are possible through a ResourceFormatLoader (W).

title: Renaming a C# file or class breaks scene references
description: Scenes reference scripts by path; renaming the .cs file without the class (or the reverse) breaks the name rule, and renaming or moving from an external IDE bypasses the editor's dependency rewrite, so scenes keep pointing at a script whose class no longer resolves.
example: Rename Player.cs to Hero.cs in Rider -> scene still references res://Player.cs; or Hero.cs still declares class Player
evidence_issues: #85274 (open, 1 reaction, 16 comments; reproduced again on 4.6.1 in a 2026-02 comment) | #116169 (closed by PR #117617 in 4.7, 12 reactions; duplicate #116812: [GlobalClass] file created in an external editor not registered until restart)
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPathAttributeGenerator.cs:56 and :97 (script path and name check are baked from the file location at compile time) | editor/docks/filesystem_dock.cpp:1701 (dependency rewrite lives in the FileSystem dock move path; that external renames bypass it is inferred, stated by a contributor in #85274)
frequency: low reactions; #85274 16 comments
fix_reason: The class-name half disappears if file = class (see CS-A-01); the path half applies to any language: a Petrichor rename refactoring in its LSP/CLI must rewrite .tscn/.tres references and .uid files, and a project check can flag dangling script paths.

title: [GlobalClass] registration depends on a built, loaded assembly
description: C# Resource and Node subclasses appear in Create Resource / Add Node only with [GlobalClass] (since 4.1) and only after a successful build has loaded the assembly; classes whose base comes from another assembly, and some native bases, have been missed.
example: [GlobalClass] public partial class Stats : Resource { [Export] public int Hp { get; set; } }  -> not listed until Build
evidence_issues: #27470 (closed by PR #72619 [GlobalClass] in 4.1, 71 reactions, 45 comments; later comment "click Build, then try again") | #116169 (closed by PR #117617 in 4.7, 12 reactions; duplicate #116812) | #95036 (open, 6 reactions, 7 comments: base class from another assembly -> not listed) | #111247 and #111990 (closed by PR #112023 in 4.6: GlobalClass extending GPUParticles2D / HTTPRequest not registered because the C# class name leaked as the base name, see CS-A-07)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_global_classes.html "Global classes show up in the Add Node and Create Resource dialogs." "Global classes are registered with the [GlobalClass] attribute."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:202-217 (global class info is read from the loaded assembly's path-to-type map; an unknown path yields no class name) | ScriptManagerBridge.cs:236-257 (base type found by walking loaded types) | ScriptManagerBridge.cs:363-374 (the editor is asked to rescan script paths only after an assembly load)
frequency: 11 topic:dotnet issues have "GlobalClass" in the title; #27470 71 reactions; several forum threads titled "custom resource not showing up in create new resource menu" (web search)
fix_reason: Petrichor's ScriptLanguageExtension::_get_global_class_name (core/object/script_language_extension.h:754) can answer from a source parse, as GDScript does, so registration never waits for a build.

title: PascalCase C# names vs snake_case engine names in string APIs
description: The C# API renames engine members (and some class names, e.g. GPUParticles2D -> GpuParticles2D) to PascalCase, but string-keyed APIs (Call, CallDeferred, Get, Set, Connect, TweenProperty) need the engine's snake_case names, while user C# methods and signals are registered under their C# PascalCase names; a wrong string fails only at run time, and the bridge itself has leaked C# class names where engine names were required.
example: CallDeferred("AddChild", n) fails, needs "add_child" or MethodName.AddChild; GDScript must call cs_node.PrintNodeName() and cs_node.MySignal.connect(f)
evidence_issues: #16872 (open, 5 reactions, 18 comments) | #82219 (open, 3 reactions: TweenProperty takes NodePath, PropertyName does not fit) | #114481 (open, 1 reaction: some PropertyName constants missing) | #28748 (closed, 4 reactions: PascalCase naming inconsistencies) | #111247 and #111990 (closed by PR #112023 in 4.6: "dotnet class lookup returning modified names instead of engine names")
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "There are some methods such as Get()/Set(), Call()/CallDeferred() and signal connection method Connect() that rely on Godot's snake_case API naming conventions. So when using e.g. CallDeferred("AddChild"), AddChild will not work"
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp:3960, :4151, :4289 (snake_to_pascal_case for engine properties, methods, signals) | modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp:3884 (class proxy names via pascal_to_pascal_case) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:255 (GodotClassNameAttribute needed to map a C# class name back to the engine name) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptMethodsGenerator.cs:165-169 (user methods registered under their C# name verbatim) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptSignalsGenerator.cs:138-139 (signal name = delegate name minus "EventHandler")
frequency: 10 topic:dotnet issues match "snake_case" (GitHub search); listed in the docs' "Current gotchas"
fix_reason: Petrichor uses the engine's names verbatim (no renaming layer), and the compiler checks literal method, property and signal names passed to string-keyed APIs against ClassDB and script metadata.

title: GDScript cannot use C# default arguments, overloads or constructor parameters
description: Calls from GDScript into C# are dispatched by (name, argument count) and C# publishes no default-argument metadata, so omitting an optional argument fails; same-arity overloads collapse to one and overloaded names lose their signature; constructors are not listed (GDScript looks for _init); generic, ref/out and non-Variant-typed methods are silently not exposed.
example: C#: public void Hit(int dmg, bool crit = false)  GDScript: cs.Hit(5) -> "Nonexistent function"; preload("res://Foo.cs").new(2) -> "Too many arguments"
evidence_issues: #59025 (open, 6 reactions, 1 comment; fix PR #119015 open since 2026-04) | #109189 (open, 0 reactions, 14 comments; duplicate #73594) | #120988 (open, confirmed on 4.6.3/4.7, static members, see CS-A-09)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html "calling C# methods from GDScript should be straightforward. The marshalling process will do its best to cast the arguments to match function signatures." (defaults, overloads and constructors not mentioned)
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1767-1782 (CSharpInstance::_callp looks up a trampoline by {name, argc}; no match -> CALL_ERROR_INVALID_METHOD) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptMethodsGenerator.cs:285 and :355-356 (defaultArguments: null) | ScriptMethodsGenerator.cs:59-62 and :137 (overloads with equal name and arity deduplicated) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2770-2777 (overloaded name -> empty MethodInfo) | ScriptMethodsGenerator.cs:134 (only MethodKind.Ordinary, so constructors are never listed) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:321-322 and :335-344 (generic methods, ref/out and non-Variant parameters dropped without diagnostic) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6007-6008, :6056-6060, :6103 (GDScript resolves constructors as _init and takes the default-argument count from the foreign script's MethodInfo)
frequency: low per issue (0-6 reactions); 67 topic:dotnet issues have "gdscript" in the title (GitHub search)
fix_reason: Petrichor's ScriptExtension must publish complete MethodInfo (default_args, an _init entry for its constructor) and apply defaults in callp, all through _get_method_info (core/object/script_language_extension.h:126); the language can avoid overloading by arity (L).

title: GDScript sees an incomplete, type-erased surface of a C# script
description: In editor builds a C# script reports only exported properties, no constants and no static members, and non-[GlobalClass] class types are reported as their native base; GDScript completion and static checks miss members or mark them unsafe, static fields cannot be read at all, and the member list differs between editor and exported builds.
example: C#: public static int Num = 42; public int Hp { get; set; }  GDScript: cs.Num -> "Invalid access"; cs.Hp works but is not completed and warns unsafe_property_access
evidence_issues: #92183 (open, 0 reactions, 10 comments; PR #96833 not merged) | #120988 (open, confirmed) | #94419 (closed 2026-09 as not reproducible on 4.7.2: returned types reported as native base) | #67167 (closed by PR #67304 in 4.2: read-only properties inaccessible) | #81683 (closed by PR #124305 in 4.8: always add class_name to properties)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html "Accessing C# fields from GDScript is straightforward, you shouldn't have anything to worry about."
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2952-2961 (editor build: get_script_property_list returns exported members only; non-editor build returns all, :2962-2976) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:3035-3040 (get_members returns exported names only) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPropertiesGenerator.cs:121 and :126 (static properties and fields excluded from the bridge) | core/object/script_language.h:196 (get_constants default is empty; CSharpScript does not override it) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:51-60 (class_name is the C# name only for [GlobalClass], otherwise the native base)
frequency: low: 5 issues found, 0-2 reactions each
fix_reason: Petrichor's ScriptExtension can report every member, constant and static member with precise class_name/enum hints via _get_script_property_list, _get_members and _get_constants; nothing beyond the GDExtension interface is needed.

title: C# reaches GDScript only through strings, and foreign Callables arrive empty
description: GDScript members are reached with Call/Get/Set/Connect on string names returning Variant; a wrong name or arity only pushes an error in debug builds (the docs say it fails silently) and never throws, GDScript instances are typed as GodotObject, and GDScript lambdas or bound Callables passed into C# become empty Callables.
example: gd.Call("print_node_name")  (missing argument, no exception)   GDScript: cs.SetCallable(func(): print("x"))  -> C# sees null::null
evidence_issues: #97358 (open, confirmed, 0 reactions, 8 comments: cannot call a GDScript-lambda Callable in C#) | #76108 (open, 2 reactions; duplicate #110419) | #77624 (open, 0 reactions, 5 comments: result of GodotObject.Call cannot be awaited)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html "You will have to use GodotObject.Get() and GodotObject.Set()." and "This line will fail silently and won't error out." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_differences.html "Custom Callables are unsupported. A Callable is custom when any of the following holds: Callable has bound information ... Callable was created from other languages through the GDExtension API."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp:533-538 ("Some other CallableCustom. We only support ManagedCallable." -> marshalled as an empty Callable) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/ExceptionUtils.cs:145-155 (call errors become GD.PushError only under [Conditional("DEBUG")], no exception) | core/object/object.cpp:696-712 (Object::call forwards to callp and returns a Variant)
frequency: low: 3 open issues plus 1 duplicate, 0-2 reactions
fix_reason: Petrichor keeps Callable and Variant as opaque engine values (custom callables are never re-marshalled), and its checker can type GDScript objects from Script.get_script_method_list / get_script_property_list (bound at core/object/script_language.cpp:178-179) instead of raw strings.

title: Typed arrays and dictionaries lose or fake their element type across the bridge
description: Before 4.4 Godot.Collections.Array<T> was untyped on the engine side, so assigning it to a GDScript Array[T] failed; the documented "convert" constructor Array<T>(Array) still only wraps the untyped array, and typed collections of C# script types raised errors after rebuilds.
example: var a = new Godot.Collections.Array<int>(untyped); gd.Set("arr", a);  with GDScript var arr: Array[int]  -> engine still sees an untyped array
evidence_issues: #103343 (closed by PR #106243 in 4.5, 22 reactions, 38 comments: "Script class can only be set together with base class name" with typed collections on rebuild) | #74936 (closed 2026-05 after PR #98545 in 4.4, 6 reactions, 7 comments) | #100070 (closed 2026-05 after PR #98545) | #96112 (closed not planned: typed array copied in cross-language calls)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_collections.html "An untyped Godot.Collections.Array can be converted to a typed array using the Godot.Collections.Array<T>(Godot.Collections.Array) constructor."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Array.cs:1100-1113 and :1136-1178 (new arrays call set_typed) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Array.cs:1188-1193 (Array<T>(Array) stores the given array without set_typed or element check, so the engine-side type is unchanged, contrary to "converted") | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Dictionary.cs:580-585 (Dictionary<TKey,TValue>(Dictionary) wraps the same way)
frequency: #103343 22 reactions; others 0-6
fix_reason: Petrichor's Array[T] can be the engine typed array itself (array_set_typed is in core/extension/gdextension_interface.json:7483), so static and engine-visible element types cannot diverge; conversion from an untyped array is a checked copy.

title: C# event subscriptions to [Signal]s are invisible to the engine
description: A [Signal] delegate generates a C# event whose += adds to a private backing delegate; the engine sees only one internal connection per signal, so += handlers are not listed, not found by IsConnected and not disconnected when the receiver is freed, and signals cannot be declared in interfaces.
example: enemy.Died += OnDied;  enemy.IsConnected(Enemy.SignalName.Died, Callable.From(OnDied)) -> false; freeing the receiver leaves a dangling handler
evidence_issues: #70414 (open, 40 reactions, 20 comments; duplicate #74984) | #76690 (open, 9 reactions, 12 comments: IsConnected wrong for custom and editor-connected signals) | #80033 (open, 8 reactions: cannot inherit signals from interfaces)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_signals.html "Connecting to a custom signal using += doesn't disconnect automatically when the receiving node is freed." and "In contrast with other C# events, you cannot use Invoke to raise events tied to Godot signals."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptSignalsGenerator.cs:289-309 (event add/remove only touch backing_<Signal>; TODO at :285-288) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1949-1963 (one EventSignalCallable per custom signal, connected to the owner itself) | modules/mono/signal_awaiter_utils.cpp:179-186 (that callable re-raises the C# event) | ScriptSignalsGenerator.cs:117-122 (signals collected only from delegates declared in the class)
frequency: #70414 40 reactions (among the most-reacted open topic:dotnet bugs)
fix_reason: .NET events are absent in Petrichor; the lesson is to make engine connect/disconnect the only subscription mechanism so connection lists, is_connected and auto-disconnect behave the same in every language.

title: Editor "connect signal" cannot generate a C# handler
description: The editor's signal-connection dialog inserts a missing handler at the last line of the file, which for C# lands after the closing brace; since 4.3 generation is simply disabled for C#, so the connection is made but no handler is written and the user must add a correctly named method by hand.
example: Connect Button.pressed in the Node dock -> scene gets a connection to _on_button_pressed, no C# method is created
evidence_issues: #18721 (open, 54 reactions, 18 comments, 24 cross-referencing issues; "fixed" in 4.3 by disabling generation, PR #87952)
evidence_source: editor/script/script_text_editor.cpp:430-434 (missing function is inserted after the last line) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:414-419 (make_function intentionally empty) | modules/mono/csharp_script.h:580 (can_make_function returns false)
frequency: #18721 54 reactions and 24 cross-referencing issues: the most-reacted open issue in this area
fix_reason: If a Petrichor file is itself the class body (no closing brace), end-of-file insertion is valid and ScriptLanguageExtension make_function suffices (script_language_extension.h:478-479); a project check can verify .tscn connections against script methods (T); a brace-delimited class would need an editor API with an insertion position (core change).

title: .NET collections, LINQ results, structs, records and Nullable<T> cannot cross to the engine
description: Only a closed list of types is marshallable; List<T>, Dictionary<K,V>, IEnumerable/LINQ results, user structs, records, plain classes, Nullable<T> and some arrays (bool[], Vector2I[], enum arrays) cannot be exported, used in signals or passed as Variant, and non-exported members or methods using them are silently not exposed.
example: [Export] public List<int> Ids = new();  -> GD0102;  public List<int> GetIds()  -> silently not callable from GDScript
evidence_issues: #70298 (open, 38 reactions, 7 comments; duplicate #105387 bool[]) | #95358 (open, 1 reaction, 7 comments: Vector2I[] rejected) | #95813 (closed not planned: enum arrays) | #19868 (open, 1 reaction, 9 comments: Nullable<float>) | godot-proposals#438 (open, 143 reactions, 21 comments: export structs) | godot-proposals#997 (open, 56 reactions: export custom System.Object/struct types)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_exports.html "only certain C# arrays and the collection types defined in the Godot.Collections namespace are Variant-compatible, therefore, only those types can be exported." but also "C# arrays can exported as long as the element type is a Variant-compatible type." (not true for bool[]/Vector2I[]) | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_collections.html "Godot only understands its own collection types, so it's required to use them when talking to the engine."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/MarshalUtils.cs:88-249 (closed type list; user structs -> null at :127-157; arrays only for listed element types at :158-208) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:329-330 and :343-344 (methods using such types dropped silently) | ExtensionMethods.cs:365-378 (properties of such types skipped silently) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/Common.cs:50-58 (GD0102 raised only for [Export])
frequency: godot-proposals#438 143 and #997 56 reactions; #70298 38 reactions
fix_reason: .NET types are absent in Petrichor, but its own structs, records and collections face the same rule -> L: every type that can cross (export, signal, script method) has a defined Variant representation, otherwise the compiler rejects it (T) instead of silently dropping the member.

title: C# interfaces have no engine representation
description: An interface type cannot be a signal parameter, an exported property type or a Variant, and signals cannot be declared in interfaces; users fall back to GodotObject plus run-time type checks.
example: [Signal] public delegate void HitEventHandler(IDamageable target);  -> GD0202;  [Export] public IDamageable Target;  -> GD0102
evidence_issues: #38188 (open, 15 reactions, 10 comments; confirmed on 4.3-dev in 2024-01) | #80033 (open, 8 reactions) | godot-proposals#8722 (open, 77 reactions: export interface types) | godot-proposals#307 (open, 26 reactions)

title: C# enums cross the bridge as bare integers
description: Variant has no implicit conversion from C# enums, so EmitSignal, Call and Variant need explicit casts, and method and signal metadata report enum parameters as plain int with no enum name, so GDScript sees int.
example: EmitSignal(SignalName.StateChanged, State.Idle)  -> compile error "Cannot convert State to Variant"; the GDScript handler parameter shows as int
evidence_issues: #67549 (closed by PR #68233 in 4.4 via generated EmitSignal<Name> methods, 9 reactions) | #28536 (closed, 11 reactions: enums in dictionary exports) | #95813 (closed not planned: enum arrays not exportable)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_variant.html "Enums are supported by Godot.Variant since their underlying type is an integer type which are all compatible. However, implicit conversions don't exist, enums must be manually converted"
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/MarshalUtils.cs:124-125 (enum -> MarshalType.Enum, an integer) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptSignalsGenerator.cs:486-493 and ScriptMethodsGenerator.cs:368-375 (class_name only for Object; no enum name, no PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_ENUM)
frequency: modest: 9-11 reactions
status: fixed for signals (PR #68233, 4.4); metadata loss open
fix_reason: Petrichor can define enum-to-int conversion at Variant boundaries (L) and report enum-typed parameters with PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_ENUM (core/object/property_info.h:109) and a qualified class_name in its ScriptExtension metadata (W).

title: async/Task methods do not map to engine coroutines
description: A C# async method returning Task is not Variant-compatible, so it is not exposed to GDScript and cannot be wrapped as a Callable (in 3.x it failed at run time as a signal handler); async void runs fire-and-forget; GDScript await on a call into C# returns immediately, and C# cannot await the result of Call on a GDScript coroutine.
example: public async Task LoadAsync()  -> not callable from GDScript;  await cs.LoadAsync() in GDScript does not wait
evidence_issues: #56468 (open, 0 reactions, 3 comments: async signal handler -> "unmarshallable managed type ... Task`1") | #77624 (open, 0 reactions, 5 comments) | #25015 (open, 0 reactions: no errors reported from async functions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_differences.html "An equivalent of awaiting a signal in GDScript can be achieved with the await keyword and GodotObject.ToSignal."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:324-330 (non-Variant return type such as Task -> method not exposed) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Callable.generics.cs:258 (Callable.From requires [MustBeVariant] TResult) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2572-2596 (GDScript await suspends only on a Signal or a GDScriptFunctionState; any other value returns immediately)
frequency: low: 3 open issues, 0 reactions
fix_reason: Task is absent in Petrichor, but for Petrichor coroutines to be awaitable from GDScript (and to await GDScript) they must surface as a Signal at the Variant boundary, which a ScriptExtension can return.

title: Exported defaults in the inspector are guessed from source, not executed
description: For non-tool scripts the editor takes exported default values from a source analysis of initializers and trivial getters; computed properties or non-constant initializers show the type default in the inspector while the running game gets another value.
example: private int _n = 2; [Export] public int N { get => _n + 3; set => _n = value - 3; }  -> inspector shows 0, game uses 5
evidence_issues: #37812 (closed by PR #56299 in 4.0, 9 reactions, 22 comments: base members reset when the derived class has [Tool]) | #80864 (open, 1 reaction, 4 comments: value initialization only works with [Tool])
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_exports.html "A property's get is not actually executed to determine the default value. Instead, Godot analyzes the C# source code." and "some properties are too complex for the analyzer to understand."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptPropertyDefValGenerator.cs:217-277 (uses the initializer if statically resolvable, else a getter returning a single field, else "default")
frequency: low; documented note
fix_reason: Petrichor can restrict exported-member defaults to compile-time constant expressions (L), or have the compiler warn when the editor-visible default cannot be computed statically (T).

title: [Tool] code sees non-tool C# objects as their native base class
description: In the editor only tool scripts are instantiated; other script objects get placeholder instances and C# wraps them as their native type, so a [Tool] script or editor plugin that casts to or exports a non-tool C# type throws InvalidCastException; users end up marking every class [Tool].
example: [Tool] partial class Spawner : Node { [Export] public EnemyData Data; }  with non-tool EnemyData : Resource  -> InvalidCastException in the editor
evidence_issues: #36395 (open, 24 reactions, 22 comments; duplicate #112085) | #85459 (open, 19 reactions, 20 comments; still reported 2026-03) | #96306 (open, 4 reactions; duplicate #115304) | #80298 (open, 2 reactions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html "any other GDScript that your tool script uses must also be a tool. The editor is not able to construct instances from GDScript files without @tool"
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2540-2554 (CSharpScript::can_instantiate: in the editor only tool scripts unless scripting is enabled) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1145-1165 (an object without a C# instance gets a managed wrapper of its native class) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2673-2675 (placeholder_instance_create)
frequency: 19 topic:dotnet issues mention InvalidCastException and Tool (GitHub search); #36395 24 and #85459 19 reactions; several forum threads (web search)
fix_reason: The placeholder model is engine behaviour; Petrichor's checker can flag tool code that downcasts to or exports non-tool script types and type such values as their native base in tool context (L), but running non-tool code in the editor would need an engine change.

title: Abstract engine classes and other-language scripts cannot be inherited
description: Engine classes registered as abstract (PhysicsBody3D, CollisionObject3D) get an internal C# constructor, so C# subclasses do not compile and scripts of any language cannot instantiate them; a C# script also cannot extend a GDScript class or the reverse.
example: public partial class MyBody : PhysicsBody3D {}  -> compile error, no accessible constructor
evidence_issues: #71834 (open, 14 reactions, 5 comments; GDScript cannot instantiate either) | #38352 (closed, 1 reaction: GDScript extending a C# script)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html "A GDScript file may not inherit from a C# script. Likewise, a C# script may not inherit from a GDScript file. Due to how complex this would be to implement, this limitation is unlikely to be lifted in the future."
evidence_source: scene/register_scene_types.cpp:736-737 (GDREGISTER_ABSTRACT_CLASS for CollisionObject3D and PhysicsBody3D) | modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp:3888 (is_instantiable requires a creation_func) | modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp:2362-2364 (non-instantiable classes get an internal constructor)
frequency: #71834 14 reactions
fix_reason: Instantiating an abstract native base needs a ClassDB constructor, and cross-language inheritance needs two script instances on one Object; a script language cannot supply either, so Petrichor can only reject these up front (T).

title: GDExtension classes have no C# type
description: C# bindings are generated from ClassDB when the engine is built, so classes registered by GDExtensions at run time have no C# proxy; their objects are wrapped as the nearest engine base and their API is reachable only through Call/Get/Set.
example: GetNode<MyExtensionNode>("X") impossible;  GetNode<Node2D>("X").Call("ext_method")
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#8191 (open, 129 reactions, 48 comments: generate C# bindings for GDExtensions) | PR #75955 (merged in 4.1: wrap extension objects as their engine base instead of throwing)
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1145-1153 (GDExtension classes are skipped up to the first engine-registered base when the managed wrapper is created; comment cites #75955)
frequency: godot-proposals#8191 129 reactions
fix_reason: Petrichor can build its type environment from ClassDB at load and edit time (ClassDB queries are bound and in the GDExtension interface) instead of a binding set frozen at engine build, so extension classes are first-class types.
